sector_model: commercial single-product biopharma: P/E and EV/earnings on GAAP, FCF after licensing payments, net cash, patent and generic entry timeline, pipeline spending, customer concentration
thesis: Harmony Biosciences (Nasdaq: HRMY) sells WAKIX (pitolisant) for narcolepsy; it is the only commercial product. Q3 2026 10-Q (full text read) and the 2026-11-04 earnings release exhibit 99.1 (read) reviewed; submissions checked 2026-11-11. Q3 net product revenue 268.9M (+12.3%), nine months 745.6M (+19.4%); estimated average patients 9,350 (+400 in Q3). 2026 WAKIX net revenue guidance reiterated at 1.0B to 1.04B. Gross margin 70.0% in Q3 and 74.7% for nine months (79.2% a year earlier). R&D rose to 71.7M in Q3 (55.0M) including a 25.0M IPR&D patent milestone (MSN license). Operating income Q3 54.2M versus 65.5M (-17%); nine months 180.8M versus 169.9M (+6%). Net income nine months 156.1M versus 136.2M; TTM net income 178.6M (FY2025 158.7M from XBRL, less 136.2M, plus 156.1M). Price 34.22 (Nasdaq close 2026-11-11, two quote publishers). Shares 58,720,081 at 2026-09-30; market cap about 2.01B; about 11.3x TTM net income. Cash 647.1M plus short-term investments 124.0M plus long-term investments 280.5M equal 1,051.6M; term loan principal 150M (5.0M due rest of 2026, 20M in 2027, 125M in 2028); net cash about 902M; EV about 1.11B. 9M operating cash flow 196.9M (222.0M a year earlier), capex nil, and license upfront payments of 32.0M (investing) so 9M cash after those is about 164.9M. TTM operating cash flow 323.0M (FY2025 348.2M less 222.0M plus 196.9M), roughly 16% of market cap before license payments, but Q4 2025 capex and license payments were not checked. Generic entry: settlements with Lupin, Novugen and Novitium allow generic sales from July 2030 if pediatric exclusivity is granted, or earlier under certain circumstances; the Orange Book patents expire September 2029 and March 2030. Pipeline: Pitolisant GR PDUFA 2027-04-01, Pitolisant HD Phase 3 data 2027, BP-205 orexin agonist Phase 1b data Q1 2027. CEO transition: Jeffrey Dayno retires 2026-12-31, Peter Anastasiou (COO) succeeds 2027-01-01.
counterthesis: A single product with a patent cliff in 2029 to 2030 means the low earnings multiple partly reflects limited remaining duration: gross margin is falling (74.7% versus 79.2%), operating costs are rising ahead of revenue (R&D +34% in nine months), and Q3 operating income fell 17% on revenue growth of 12%. Revenue growth already slowed from 19% in nine months to 12% in Q3. Three specialty pharmacies make up 100% of gross receivables (CVS Caremark 42%, Accredo 38%, PANTHERx 20%), so a payer or channel change would bite. Nine month interest income of 21.3M flatters pretax profit, and the large cash pile is only valuable if deployed well: management says it will pursue business development, and a large acquisition or licensing deal would change the picture (nine month IPR&D and license payments already total 74M or more). The stock fell 12% between 2026-11-03 (37.02) and 2026-11-05 (32.47) after results and the CEO news; I did not establish why beyond the figures above. BP-205 and Pitolisant GR may not succeed, and competing orexin agonists from larger companies could displace WAKIX. The strong TTM cash flow does not subtract future spending on R&D that is likely to rise. A cheap multiple on a patent-limited single product is not by itself a margin of safety.
invalidation: Quarterly WAKIX revenue growth falling below about 5%, patient adds below 300 per quarter, loss of generic settlement protections or earlier generic entry, gross margin below 70% on a sustained basis, a large cash-funded acquisition that destroys value, or competitor orexin agonist approval that displaces WAKIX. Supportive: continued 400 patient adds, Pitolisant GR approval in April 2027 extending exclusivity, and disciplined capital deployment.
